text:
emma.support: Hey team — customer ACME reports repeated mid-stream SSE disconnects when users switch between metro public WiFi and their phone hotspot. Happens ~30s after swap, stream closes with partial output, app shows 'stream closed'. Ticket CS-8972. 5 users so far.

raj.engineering: Thanks. Any error codes in the client or server logs? Is token rotation happening during the swap?

emma.support: Client logs show `ECONNRESET` and then `EOF`. Customer says they rotate tokens every 10m, but swaps happen during active stream (not at rotation boundary). No 401s observed.

olivia.mobile: Repro steps I got from them:
1) Start SSE stream from iOS app (we use EventSource polyfill)
2) While streaming, toggle Personal Hotspot on phone to connect laptop -> network switches carrier->wifi
3) After ~20-40s stream cuts, last chunk incomplete (truncated JSON).

They provided this trimmed client snippet:
```
const es = new EventSource(urlWithToken);
es.onmessage = e => handleChunk(e.data);
es.onerror = e => console.log('es error', e);
// they don't send heartbeats from client
```

olivia.mobile: They also shared our server-side tail: `net/http: connection reset by peer` and nginx proxy logs `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream`.

raj.engineering: Sounds like TCP reset due to NAT mapping change / different IP after hotspot. When the mobile switches tethering, many carriers tear flows. Two quick asks: a) can we get a raw curl repro the customer used? b) confirm whether they're using our streaming SSE proxy (yes/no).

emma.support: They used curl -N and saw same behaviour. They are on hosted API (streaming via our edge proxy).

oncall-bot: Incident CS-8972 (priority P2) created and paged oncall. Link: https://incidents.redwood/CS-8972

alex-sre: Confirming: this is a classic mid-stream TCP reset after NAT rebind. Proxy sees reset and returns 502/empty; backend may have already produced partial data. Two mitigation suggestions:
- Recommend client implement short keepalive comments (SSE comment `: heartbeat` every 15s) to keep NAT mappings alive during network flaps.
- On server/proxy, increase `proxy_read_timeout` and enable `proxy_force_close` handling to avoid half-closed sockets causing truncated chunks.

raj.engineering: Also check if our token rotation code triggers a reconnect — if client recreates EventSource mid-stream without resuming, they will lose spot. We should document resume strategies (client should store last event id / last token and request continuation).

tim-frontend: Quick Q: customer worried about billing — are partial streamed tokens billed?

emma.support: I told them billing only for tokens successfully delivered. If stream truncated we charge for delivered tokens up to that point. Escalating to billing for clarity.

olivia.mobile: Repro curl we were sent (works to reproduce the disconnect):
```bash
curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=x"
# then toggle hotspot/wifi on phone
```

raj.engineering: Thanks. Can we get a packet-level capture from the client when they repro? If not possible, logs showing the delta time between last chunk and socket close would help.

emma.support: Customer can provide tcpdump next time. For now they uploaded edge logs (attached in ticket) showing sequence: request -> 12 tokens -> reset -> 0-length chunk.

alex-sre: Short-term workaround for them: implement client-side incremental checkpointing — buffer last complete sentence/last token index and on reconnect re-request with a prompt prefix to continue. Also set EventSource/Fetch to auto-retry with backoff.

tim-frontend: Can we add a small note in docs: "mobile/network handoff can produce mid-stream resets — best practices: heartbeats, idempotent resumes, exponential reconnect"?

raj.engineering: I'll open an internal RFC to add content about network handoffs + SSE semantics. Also will check proxy config for `tcp_nodelay` and `keepalive` settings.

emma.support: Customer accepted workaround for now (client heartbeat + retry). They've asked for ETA on server-side hardening. Can we estimate?

alex-sre: We can try a conservative proxy timeout bump and enable connection probing in the edge config — low-risk, could be rolled in 48-72h. I'll PR a config change and flag for canary.

oncall-bot: alex-sre scheduled canary deploy for edge-proxy config change (CS-8972). Canary in 1 hour.

olivia.mobile: Adding final note for reproducibility: iOS 15.4, EventSource polyfill v1.2. Customer hotspot uses AT&T; carrier NAT rebind observed.

emma.support: Great — marking ticket P2, assigning follow-up to raj & alex. I'll keep customer updated. :thumbsup:
